audit_findings.title: The anchor may omit the full recurring interest burden of the current capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed net interest expense was $141.7 million in H1 2026 versus $145.5 million in H1 2025, while FY2025 expense was $292.8 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any post-tax interest omitted from the equity-level OE anchor increases forecast OE and every scenario value because debt principal is not deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: However, we expect that these favorable items may be partially offset by the impact from inflation, investments in our U.S. commercial sales channel, higher net interest expense and a higher estimated effective tax rate due to favorable 2025 adjustments that are not expected to recur.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential mismatch is not a demonstrated error. Management forecasts higher full-year net interest expense, but the latest reported six-month expense was $3.8 million lower year over year. The record does not reconcile the $974.7 million anchor to current coupons, swaps and cash interest, so it cannot establish whether the conservative anchor already absorbs the current burden or by how much.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile normalized post-tax interest from the $7,479.0 million June 2026 debt schedule, coupons, swaps and current cash interest to the interest embedded in the anchor, then rerun OE and all scenarios for any difference without deducting debt principal.

audit_findings.title: Debt-like acquisition earn-outs are absent from the common-equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $244.6 million recorded liability, equal to $1.23 per valuation share and 1.7% of base equity value; $720 million maximum equals $3.63 per share and 5.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash-settled contingent consideration is a senior claim that should reduce the equity bridge; stock-settled consideration belongs in fully diluted shares, while remeasurement gains or losses should not replace settlement economics in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, the range of our potential contingent consideration payments are $25 million to $795 million as of December 31, 2025, that may be paid out through 2031.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but it does not change the present valuation conclusion. Even deducting the filed $720 million aggregate maximum would reduce values rather than close the $18.80 gap between the $98.07 market price and the $79.27 bull value, or the $48.23 gap to the $49.84 buy-below price. It nevertheless overstates each reported intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Update the June 2026 liability through the valuation date, separate cash from stock settlement, deduct the cash claim, add future shares to dilution, reverse inconsistent remeasurement noise from OE, and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Technology reinvestment may be omitted while its amortization is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified maintenance portion; filed technology-intangible cash outflows were $103.4 million in 2023, $153.0 million in 2024, $52.4 million in 2025 and $101.2 million in H1 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back intangible amortization without subtracting recurring technology-rights or software investment inflates OE and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025 we paid $1,393.2 million, net of cash acquired, for the acquisitions of Paragon 28 and Monogram, as well as paid $52.4 million related to the ownership rights or to gain access to various technologies that were recognized as intangible assets.
audit_findings.explanation: Omission from OE is not demonstrated because the supplied record does not show the maintenance-capex calculation or distinguish replacement spending from expansion. The recurring filed outflows are potentially significant: the 2023-2025 average of $102.9 million equals 10.6% of the $974.7 million anchor, but only the maintenance portion is an OE deduction.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized technology rights, internal-use software and related payments for every OE year; classify the maintenance portion using product lives, renewals and replacement evidence; subtract it from OE and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE may retain nonrecurring tax benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified anchor effect; filed ETR was 4.0% in 2023, 12.7% in 2024, 15.1% in 2025 and 21.3% in H1 2026; the 6.2-point 2025-to-H1-2026 difference applied to 2025 pretax earnings is $51.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Discrete tax benefits retained in after-tax OE raise historical observations, the log-trend anchor and all resulting present values.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2024, the ETR was primarily driven by the foreign rate differential and a net favorable impact of changes to unrecognized tax benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate unusually favorable historical tax items and a materially higher current tax rate, but they do not establish which items were retained in the OE series. The computed $51.5 million scale is 5.3% of the anchor, yet it is not an established adjustment because the sustainable tax base and the anchor's existing tax normalization are unknown.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct cash taxes for all ten OE years, remove reserve releases, valuation-allowance changes and transaction-specific items, apply a sustainable jurisdictional tax rate, and rerun the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Contractual acquisition-share issuance may sit outside the dilution ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: no more than $62.9 million of the original Embody contingent-consideration cap remained after disclosed 2024-2025 settlements, equivalent to at most approximately 0.64 million shares at $98.07 or 0.32% of the 198.112689 million-share denominator
audit_findings.mechanism: Unincluded acquisition shares dilute value per share; any cash alternative instead reduces the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Contingent payments related to our acquisition of Embody, Inc. (“Embody”) in February 2023 are to be settled by issuance of our common stock and cash payments.
audit_findings.explanation: Exclusion from the supplied dilution ceiling is unresolved, but the filed contractual cap bounds the possible effect. Embody's $120.0 million maximum less $57.1 million of disclosed 2024-2025 stock and cash settlements leaves no more than $62.9 million before considering any 2026 settlement. Even an all-stock settlement at the valuation price would add only about 0.32% to diluted shares and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the remaining Embody milestone schedule and settlement formula, confirm any H1 2026 settlement, and add the exact maximum shares or cash claim to the denominator or bridge.

audit_findings.title: The mature-business growth model does not match the pre-revenue Monogram perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $131.5 million filed IPR&D asset, $201.6 million acquisition-date contingent liability and up to $570 million of Monogram contingent payments; development cash needs and commercialization value are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A single growth rate applied to historical OE may omit Monogram development spending and milestone claims while also failing to capture commercialization upside; both the OE forecast and equity bridge can be affected.
audit_findings.evidence: The Monogram robotic technologies are currently not commercialized and therefore have been recognized as an IPR&D intangible asset.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because Monogram is owned and its claims exist, while the model records no separate perimeter treatment. Materiality remains unresolved: the filed amounts show meaningful committed economics, but neither remaining development cash nor probability-weighted commercial cash flows are supplied. The direction is mixed because omitted costs and claims overstate value while omitted successful commercialization could understate it.
audit_findings.action: Build a separate probability-weighted Monogram model covering development cash, regulatory failure, commercialization, revenue economics and milestone payments, then combine it consistently with the legacy-business OE valuation or exclude both its asset and related claims.
